Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Browser qualification

8 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

plan.json declares the sample populations and bounds before operation timing. tests/box3d_web/contract.json owns the unchanged acceptance thresholds. The game emits telemetry only when explicitly launched with profile=1|2|3|4 or DOCKYARD_PROFILE=1|2|3|4. Mode 1 emits batches during play. Mode 2 stores at most 65536 rows in an SDK-metered allocation and emits them after successful Room/Session close, then frees the allocation before checked cleanup statistics. The ordinary game leaves telemetry disabled. Each row times the entire existing public Room.frame or Session.frame call with Godot's monotonic microsecond clock. No timing overhead is subtracted. Buffered fields contain values with stable lifetimes.

Rows include the before/after head, confirmation, generation, serial and actual repair counter. Eight-step repair samples require exactly one committed repair and actual planned/executed counts of eight. Bootstrap, pump, replacement, other repair depths, multiple-step advances, errors and outliers remain in the raw console file. The sampler has a fixed capacity and reports overflow.

run.py reuses the existing local Room/Party/TURN runner. It runs two independent installed browser processes through real production canvas widgets and collects raw operation batches, presentation intervals, visibility changes, timer deltas, linear-memory observations, real selected ICE routes and actual five-part final state/acknowledgement/cleanup evidence. It does not install a test autoload. Select Q1_BROWSER=chrome or Q1_BROWSER=firefox. Use a fresh output directory and a separate copied service project; do not rebuild the service used by an interactive game or run simultaneous benchmark actors on shared Native inputs. Select Q1_BUFFERED=1 for mode 2, as declared in buffered-plan.json.

An example inside the development shell, with absolute paths filled in:

Shell
Q1_BROWSER=chrome python3 -B tests/replay_dockyard/qualification/run.py \
  --production-ui --export-record "$EXPORT_RECORD" \
  --service-record "$SERVICE_RECORD" --out "$NEW_OUTPUT" \
  --godot "$GODOT" --ticks 1800 --turnserver "$COTURN" --provider
python3 -B tests/replay_dockyard/qualification/assess.py "$NEW_OUTPUT" \
  --out "$NEW_OUTPUT/assessment.json"

The optional --turn-bind-address selects a specific private IPv4 interface for the owned local relay; its default is loopback. It does not establish public Internet reachability. Browser security preferences are not disabled. Firefox does not accept Chromium's clipboard permission names through BiDi. On this macOS reference host its real Copy button is observed using pbpaste, with the original clipboard restored using pbcopy; the page implementation and the production invitation validation remain intact.

Set Q1_SOAK=1 and --ticks 36600 for the declared sustained case in soak-plan.json. It attempts the real host NEXT JOB widget after 90 seconds and then every 10 seconds, requires actual round/layout progression, and checks at least 600 seconds from the real GO to SAMPLE_OPERATION_END, emitted before close and telemetry serialization. Older artifacts use the checked result marker. A buffered run must have exactly one end marker and retain every operation row in sequence; teardown emission cannot extend measured play time. It retains the first result-panel screenshot and every input attempt. It does not write Game fields or replace the production action path.

Cold-load admission uses cold_usable_menu_ms, which includes visual preparation and stored-membership readiness. The earlier cold_lobby_ms backend marker is retained separately. The Compatibility renderer draws the real effects during loading before crew enrollment can acquire a live lease. Tethers and confetti share the dock's opaque material family; this does not add physics bodies.

The assessor uses nearest-rank quantiles in milliseconds and retains all rows. An incomplete population or short duration cannot pass the whole contract. The complete producer transfer is observed through public complete_inspect; the entire attachment is a conservative upper bound on its Native payload, not an exact Native byte measurement. Memory readings are sampled values, with the existing Native admission limit and cleanup checks assessed separately. Browser presentation intervals include startup stalls and live logging work. All raw intervals remain available; the end marker separates teardown intervals from the measured presentation population. Terminal Wasm memory is also read after emission so linear-memory growth during serialization is retained. The operation boundary does not include separately called presentation/getter APIs.

The later telemetry experiment retained all 73798 rows from a 610-second Firefox 159.0.1/Chrome pair and passed Native/Web cleanup. Its Firefox normal maximum was 29.56 ms against the unchanged 10 ms limit. Buffered telemetry did not resolve the rare stalls, whose cause remains unknown. The earlier candidate report and packaged review archive retain their own hashes and measurements; this experiment does not relabel them or admit a release.

The Snapshot signature reuse experiment checks work reduction separately from latency. Its Native fixture counts actual solver-part materializations, compares all five parts and the complete wire against the standalone encoder, confirms driver/observer state, and checks corrupt-header fallback, serialization failure and balanced resources. Run it with a built Native archive in the development shell:

Shell
odin test tests/replay_dockyard/qualification/tx_signature \
  -collection:godot="$PWD" -define:BOX3D_LIBRARY="$NATIVE_ARCHIVE" \
  -define:ODIN_TEST_THREADS=1 -define:ODIN_TEST_FANCY=false

The declared short browser comparison still rejects the original maximum: 30.600 ms baseline and 18.299 ms candidate. Host p95 is 3.799 ms versus 3.800 ms, so a latency gain is not established. Correct complete state and less duplicate encoding work do not qualify that candidate. A sustained run was not repeated after its short case had already violated the unchanged threshold.

Mode 3 (Q1_INTERNAL_PHASES=1 in the diagnostic driver) enables the existing stateless network profiling clock on the ready authority and reads cumulative profile metrics around each whole call. It also binds the current external transaction profiler to Godot monotonic microseconds converted to nanoseconds; the installed freestanding core:time fallback otherwise returns zero. This override is diagnostic only and is recorded as external_godot_clock. Callback presence alone must never turn an unsupported zero interval into a zero-cost claim. The clock validation covers actual Native and Web actors with state agreement and cleanup. Slow rows get a matching SAMPLE_OPERATION_PHASES record; SAMPLE_PHASE_TOTALS precedes checked close. The phases are nested or partial: Advance times r.advance, Pump times its network pump, and the complete-physics outbound route does not necessarily use the ordinary Snapshot metrics. A zero sample count means unobserved work, not zero cost. Never sum or subtract these phases into an adjusted call budget. Epoch/role replacement, total regressions and clock errors invalidate the phase sample. This mode is diagnostic and cannot qualify the uninstrumented contract. The external transaction profiler additionally reports open, model-scope and staged-capture totals/counts/clock errors. They aggregate repeated replay steps within the most recent transaction. The model scope includes its callback and accepted-action savepoints; staged capture does not duplicate those nested savepoint captures. Disabled clocks leave phases unobserved. Backend failures stay in the operation result and are independent of profiling-clock errors.

Mode 4 (Q1_COUNTERS=1) samples existing host counters before the start clock and after the end clock, with no additional clocks or counter updates inside Room.frame. A separate SAMPLE_OPERATION_COUNTERS sidecar matches every row by sequence. Its 128-row value buffer is allocated only in this mode, metered by the SDK, and freed during close. The diagnostic cannot qualify the ordinary timing contract and cannot be combined with the other probes.

next_id deltas count successful transfer preparations. Transfer slot tick, stored bytes, part progress and waiting state are snapshots, not cumulative send counters. Peer slot details require exactly one remote peer and stable scope. Server packet/byte totals describe gameplay transport; fragmentation adds raw RTC messages. Host executed_steps=0 is an unavailable client repair metric, not evidence that the host did no work. Lease wall/monotonic deltas span clock observations and must not replace the measured whole-call duration.

The frame egress regression reproduces a delayed ACK with a pump-before-step Snapshot for the old head and a separate new-head fact. It checks one current-head materialization, normative complete-wire equality, real receiver confirmation, zero-step flushing, permit refusal and balanced resources. The default standalone pump behavior remains unchanged. This work reduction is separate from the unresolved strict maximum and requires actual browser validation before any latency claim.

Q1_GECKO_PROFILE=1 enables the installed Firefox startup CPU sampler only in the owned isolated browser processes. It retains four million entries at a one-millisecond sampling interval and writes per-actor gecko-profile.json on normal browser shutdown. profile_summary.py reads those files without starting processes, reports their retained ring-buffer ranges and leaves unresolved frames explicit. Such a run is marked CPU_PROFILER_DIAGNOSTIC_NOT_ADMISSION; its timing cannot qualify the unprofiled contract. A failure to reproduce a rare spike while sampling does not establish its cause or erase the earlier failure.

Q1_TRACE_FIRST_SLOW=1 stops an owned profiler diagnostic after the first normal whole-call row over 10 ms. It records a browser clock marker and requests checked Engine shutdown before closing the browsers, preserving the sampler's recent window. trace-plan.json declares this trigger; the stopped diagnostic does not claim a complete round, final five-part comparison, or qualification pass. trigger_summary.py reads the retained profile and reports nearby samples and markers with explicit console-delivery and sampling uncertainty. Its four format tests cover sparse rows and split marker boundaries, whose unused time fields must not be interpreted as real intervals.

The broad Q1_TRACE_SYSTEM experiment is archived and rejected by the active runner after malformed, incomplete and failed-save recording attempts. Q1_PROCESS_STATE=1 instead uses a companion owned-process controller with process-state.controller.json, ready, stop, saved and failed handshakes. The runner waits for terminal status while that exact controller is alive. It is not a standalone option without the companion. process_state.py samples one verified-owned process through read-only proc_pidinfo, retaining at most 8192 rows and 8 MiB. Its CPU counters include every thread, use the observed Mach timebase, and are calibrated against the observer's process clock before measurement. They are an upper bound for game-thread CPU, not exact call CPU. The first bounded observer run saved about 800 KB cleanly but captured no slow call; it cannot attribute a missing event. Never replace missing trace data or a wait timeout with a scheduling-cause claim. See the retained causal trace observations, including failed recording attempts and unresolved clock alignment.

Q1_SHADER_DIAGNOSTIC=1 on the startup probe records transparent WebGL method durations and shader feature summaries through the real visual-preparation marker, without online configuration. It is a graphics startup diagnosis, not multiplayer or frame-budget qualification. Its own earlier failed setup and subsequent corrections remain separate records.

capability.py and automation_probe.py record bounded startup and automation prerequisites only. They do not qualify multiplayer, complete state or frame performance. Actual Safari requires its own working automation prerequisite and actual runtime evidence before admission; WebKit emulation is separate.

Keep failed attempts, raw files, cold starts, browser versions, source/tool and artifact hashes alongside the assessment. Local functional success does not complete the separate public-endpoint, human co-op review or release gates.
